newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off on strike fears, wage rises.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off on strike fears, wage rises.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange ended lower for a second session as investors nervously eyed strike threats and wage increases associated with a planned increase in gasoline prices, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 2.14 percent to 9,478.43, as 35 stocks fell, seven rose and five closed flat.
The planned 27 percent gasoline price increase set for Thursday has brought the government into conflict with companies over salary increases and with unions resisting the hike.
"The market is nervous due to reports of strikes against the gasoline price hike," said Valores Vencred broker Geronimo Paolini.
The government has said it will raise gasoline prices Thursday provided that private sector companies raise wages.
"Locally there's a lack of confidence due to what is being heard about strikes and wage hikes in the private sector," said Gabriel Osio of the Econoinvest brokerage.
Volume was heavy with 1,380 trades for 28.981 billion bolivars ($58.7 million).

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas fell 13.00 bolivars to 817.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV fell 31.00 bolivars to 3,080.00 bolivars and medium sized bank Banco Union dropped another 400.00 bolivars to 1,400 bolivars.
Brokers said the market would remain jittery and likely continue to fall while the implementation of and reaction to the planned gasoline price remained in doubt.
They added, however, that the underlying trend of the market was firm and that the market would resume its bullish tendency as soon as the gasoline hike had been resolved.
